newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end higher, spreads tighten.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end higher, spreads tighten.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Tuesday, boosted by hopes that Moody's Investors Service will upgrade the country's credit-rating soon.
The market rose amid thin client activity, with traders dominating play.
"There was a fairly significant amount of spread tightening without client flows," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's Par Brady bond was up 1/4 at 74-3/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.50 at 119.40.
Prices were mainly propelled by talk that Moody's will upgrade Argentina -- a rumor that has surfaced intermittently ever since Moody's recently rated Ecuador at B1, the same level as Argentina.
"It is very difficult to put a timing on it (an upgrade)," said Tulio Vera, managing director of emerging markets research at Bear Stearns in New York.
"My own feeling is that it will happen. It could happen today or in three months - surely before year-end," he added.
He added though, that credit ratings seldom change ratings ahead of elections. Argentina faces mid-term Congressional elections in October.
In the money markets, the three-month peso BAIBOR, the Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, rose to 7.1250 percent from 7.0625 percent.
